title: The face grows bright
hookLine: in the company of the holy the face grows bright and filth is washed

lines: TELL ME WHO YOUR FRIENDS ARE.
WE SOAK UP WHO WE SIT WITH.
cards: There's an old saying: tell me who your friends are, and I'll tell you who you are. Parents say a version of it to teenagers; coaches say it to athletes.

Underneath it is something plain: we soak up the people we sit with, their words, their moods, their habits, the jokes we start telling the way they tell them. Guru Arjan says it too, and he says it as good news.
The first stanza of ashtpadi seven begins with a face that changes.

teach.b: Saadh, you met yesterday: a holy person. Sangat is company, the people you're with. Together, saadh sangat: the company of the holy.

For Sikhs, sangat on its own also names the congregation, the people sitting together before the Guru Granth Sahib. The stanza opens: saadh kai sang mukh oojal hot. In the company of the holy, the face becomes bright.
In Punjabi, a bright face is also a way of talking about honor, the opposite of a face blackened with shame. So you look lighter, and you can hold your head up. Then: saadhsang mal sagalee khot.
In the holy company, all the filth is washed off.
Mal is grime, the kind that builds up without your noticing. Neither line says the holy company scrubs you. It's quieter than that.
You sit with good people and some of their brightness rubs off on your face. You spend time where the Name is sung, and the grime you didn't know you were carrying starts to loosen.
The stanza doesn't make it a matter of rules or effort.
It describes it the way you'd describe sunlight: sit in it and you warm up. That's why, for Sikhs, going to the sangat matters, not just reading alone.
The company is part of the medicine.

how: Sikhs speak of the sangat, the congregation gathered before the Guru Granth Sahib, as the saadh sangat, and Sikh teaching encourages joining it, not only practicing alone.

o: a hymn sung by the whole congregation
a holy person who lives alone in prayer
the company of the holy, the gathered sangat

games.q: the face grows bright — tap the pairs.

s: the stanza says the holy company scrubs you clean by force
it's quieter: like sitting in sunlight, the grime loosens.

the opposite of a face blackened with shame.

games.q: you've had a heavy week and feel grimy inside. by ashtpadi seven, where do you go?
o: stay home alone until you feel clean.
sit in good company, where the Name is sung.
argue with someone to let it out.
games.why: saadh kai sang mukh oojal hot: in the holy company the face grows bright, and the grime washes off.

practice: Picture someone good you could spend time with, a call, a walk, a meal, and imagine you're already beside them. Let your face relax, the forehead, the eyes, the mouth, the way a face does in good company; it already knows how.
If you pray, you can ask to be good company for someone else, too.

wordCard.voice: Saadh sangat. The company of the holy, where, the stanza says, the face grows bright and the grime washes off.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: saadh sangat, the company of the holy; for Sikhs, the gathered congregation.

carryVoice: Your line: company shapes you. Good company works the way sunlight does, with no scrubbing at all. Until tomorrow.

sources.work: Guru Granth Sahib (Guru Arjan, Gauri Sukhmani)
